candidates.exact_span:
Placement of sewage sludge shall not contaminate an aquifer. This shall be demonstrated through one of the following:

       a. Results of a ground-water monitoring program developed by a qualified ground-water
          scientist.
       b. A certification by a qualified ground-water scientist may be used to demonstrate that sewage
          sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit does not contaminate an aquifer.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether groundwater monitoring is required versus whether certification alone suffices affects applicable monitoring obligations (B). Different interpretations of which demonstration path applies also change what evidence is adequate for no-result or missing-monitoring cases (C).

candidates.exact_span: When a cover is placed on an active surface disposal site, the concentration of methane gas in air in any structure within the surface disposal site shall not exceed 25% of the lower explosive limit for methane gas during the period that the sewage sludge unit is active. The concentration of methane gas in air at the property line of the surface disposal site shall not exceed the lower explosive limit for methane gas during the period that the sewage sludge unit is active.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These passages set enforceable numeric methane concentration limits at two locations (structure interior and property line), referenced to the lower explosive limit. Interpretation of when the cover condition applies, what counts as a structure or property line, and how LEL is defined could change which limit applies and whether a reported measurement exceeds it.

Continuous monitoring is an explicit monitoring obligation tied to the methane limits. Whether continuous monitoring was required, and how gaps or missing readings are classified, directly affects monitoring-obligation evaluation (B) and missing-evidence semantics for periods without ordinary numeric results (C).

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested once during the life of the permit within one year from the effective date of the permit in accordance with the method specified at 40 CFR 268, Appendix I (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP)) or other approved methods. Sludge shall be tested after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The once-per-permit-life timing, one-year window from permit effective date, TCLP method requirement, and point of sampling (after final treatment, before leaving the POTW site) define when TCLP testing was required. Different readings of these conditions change whether a monitoring obligation applied in a given FY2025 period.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 261, shall be handled according to RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part262. The disposal of sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste, in other than a certified hazardous waste disposal facility shall be prohibited.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Hazardous-waste determination following TCLP governs whether RCRA disposal standards and prohibitions apply instead of ordinary sludge surface-disposal limits. Interpretation of when sludge is 'determined to be a hazardous waste' affects both which enforceable limits govern disposal (A) and what follow-on handling and reporting obligations apply (B).

candidates.exact_span: The Information Management Section, telephone no. (214) 665-6750, and the appropriate state agency shall be notified of test failure within 24 hours. A written report shall be provided to this office within 7 days after failing the TCLP.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These are event-triggered reporting obligations contingent on TCLP test failure. Whether a failure occurred and whether the 24-hour/7-day reporting requirements were applicable monitoring/reporting duties depends on interpretation of 'test failure' and timing relative to FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested at the frequency show below in Element 2, Section I.D. for PCBs. Any sludge exceeding a concentration of 50 mg/Kg shall not be surface disposed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 50 mg/Kg PCB concentration is an enforceable numeric limit for surface disposal (A). The testing frequency is incorporated by cross-reference to Element 2, Section I.D., so resolving that reference is necessary to determine when PCB monitoring was required (B).

candidates.exact_span: All sewage sludge that is disposed of in a surface disposal site shall be treated by either the Class A or Class B pathogen requirements unless sewage sludge is placed on an active surface disposal site, and is covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The daily-cover exception determines whether Class A or Class B pathogen treatment—and associated monitoring/reporting—is required versus an alternative Class C (daily cover) pathway. Interpretation of 'covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day' changes applicable monitoring obligations (B) and how missing or non-numeric pathogen evidence is classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: When reporting on the DMR, list pathogen reduction level attained as A, B, or C (daily cover). When reporting how compliance was met, list Alternative 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 for Class A, or Alternative Number 1, 2, 3, or 4 for Class B, on DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: DMR reporting codes tie observed evidence to specific compliance pathways. How these reporting fields are interpreted affects whether required pathogen monitoring/reporting was satisfied (B) and whether absent or ambiguous DMR entries represent documented no-data, conditional non-requirement, or missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Six alternatives are available to demonstrate compliance with Class A sewage sludge. All 6 alternatives require either the density of fecal coliform in the sewage sludge be less than 1000 MPN per gram of total solids (dry weight basis), or the density of Salmonella sp.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The fecal coliform density threshold is an enforceable numeric limit for Class A compliance (A). Selection among the six Class A alternatives (and the truncated Salmonella criterion) determines which monitoring demonstrations were required to establish compliance (B).
